# lightdash_user_attribute (Resource)

Manages a Lightdash user attribute in the organization, together with the values assigned to groups and users. User attributes are referenced by name from dbt, for example `required_attributes` to restrict access to dimensions and tables, and `${lightdash.attributes.<name>}` in `sql_filter` for row-level filtering.

This resource is authoritative for the whole user attribute. The Lightdash API replaces the definition, the group values and the user values at once, so any value assigned outside of Terraform, such as in the Lightdash UI, is removed on the next apply. Manage each user attribute with a single `lightdash_user_attribute` resource.

Lightdash combines the values that a user gets from `users` and from the `groups` they belong to. See the [Lightdash documentation](https://docs.lightdash.com/workspace-admin/user-attributes) for how the values and `attribute_defaults` are resolved.

It requires Lightdash 0.3243.0 or later, which added multiple values per user attribute. The resource always sends the `values` and `attributeDefaults` fields of the API, which older versions don't have.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "lightdash_group" "sales_us" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "sales_us"
  members           = []
}

resource "lightdash_group" "sales_emea" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "sales_emea"
  members           = []
}

# A user attribute with values assigned to groups
resource "lightdash_user_attribute" "region" {
  name        = "region"
  description = "The sales regions that a user can see"

  # Used for users who don't have their own value
  attribute_defaults = ["none"]

  groups = [
    {
      group_uuid = lightdash_group.sales_us.group_uuid
      values     = ["us"]
    },
    {
      group_uuid = lightdash_group.sales_emea.group_uuid
      values     = ["uk", "de", "fr"]
    },
  ]

  # Values can be assigned to individual users too
  users = [
    {
      user_uuid = "xxxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx"
      values    = ["us", "uk"]
    },
  ]
}

# A user attribute without any values
resource "lightdash_user_attribute" "is_admin" {
  name = "is_admin"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the user attribute. It is the name referenced from dbt, such as `required_attributes` and `${lightdash.attributes.<name>}`.

### Optional

- `attribute_defaults` (Set of String) The default values for users who don't have their own value in this user attribute. Omit it to have no default values. It must not be an empty set.
- `description` (String) The description of the user attribute. It defaults to an empty string.
- `groups` (Attributes Set) The values of the user attribute assigned to groups. This is authoritative, so group values that are not in the configuration are removed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--groups))
- `users` (Attributes Set) The values of the user attribute assigned to users. This is authoritative, so user values that are not in the configuration are removed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--users))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier. It is computed as `organizations/<organization_uuid>/user-attributes/<user_attribute_uuid>`.
- `organization_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Lightdash organization that the user attribute belongs to.
- `user_attribute_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Lightdash user attribute.

<a id="nestedatt--groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `groups`

Required:

- `group_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Lightdash group, which must belong to the organization. It must be written in lowercase.
- `values` (Set of String) The values of the user attribute for the group. At least one value is required.


<a id="nestedatt--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `users`

Required:

- `user_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Lightdash user, who must be a member of the organization. It must be written in lowercase.
- `values` (Set of String) The values of the user attribute for the user. At least one value is required.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# User attributes can be imported by specifying the resource identifier.
terraform import lightdash_user_attribute.example "organizations/${organization_uuid}/user-attributes/${user_attribute_uuid}"
```
